About.title: Learn at your own pace
About.intro: AIDevCourse is a free reading space for people learning to work with AI on code. You do not need an account to read.
About.storage: Achievements and your last lesson are saved in this browser on this domain. Translations of the same course share achievements. Clearing browser data or changing devices or domains may remove access to these records. Learning records are not sent to the site server.
About.languages: The interface is available in five languages. Each language publishes its own lessons, so the library can differ. A functional cookie remembers your language choice; explicit language URLs work even when cookies are blocked.
About.privacy: There are no advertising or analytics scripts. External links lead to other services with their own policies. The hosting provider may keep ordinary access logs. Never paste private keys or sensitive project information into public examples.

announcements.initialize: Set initial a and b values for each candidate. There is no input or prediction yet.
announcements.predict: The model assigns “{target}” a probability of {before}%. Next, compare with the source.
announcements.compare: The source answer is “{target}”, but the model assigns it only {before}%. Use the source answer to measure the prediction gap.
announcements.update: The original model stays visible beside the adjusted model. With the same input, a and b change the scores, and the probability of {target} rises from {before}% to {after}%.

static.initialize: Initialize each candidate’s parameters. For example, “{target}” has a = {a} and b = {b}.
static.predict: Enter “{input}…”, represent rain as x = {x}, and predict the next token: {summary}.
static.compare: Compare with the source, “{source}”. The next token is “{target}”.
static.update: Adjust the parameters from the gap. For “{target}”, a changes from {a} to {nextA}, and b from {b} to {nextB}. Input x remains {x}. The score changes from {score} to {nextScore}, and the Softmax probability from {before}% to {after}%.
static.multiple: In each round, compare with the source answer, “{target}”, adjust the parameters from the gap, and predict again.

Training.comparisonLabel: The gap between this prediction and the source

Pretraining.label: An overview of pretraining
Pretraining.cleaningDescription: Collect data from code repositories such as GitHub, books, technical documentation, and Stack Overflow Q&A. Deduplicate it and filter out low-quality or unsuitable content to produce training text.
Pretraining.tokensDescription: A tokenizer splits “{text}” into tokens and maps them to token IDs: {tokens}.
Pretraining.predictionDescription: Predict the next token → compare with the source → adjust parameters → predict again. Repeat this training loop. Comparison uses the next token in the original text; updated parameters are used for the next prediction.

Newton.label: Interactive Newton’s second law demo
Newton.title: Try it: Newton’s second law
Newton.equationExact: Acceleration equals {force} newtons divided by {mass} kilograms, or {acceleration} meters per second squared
Newton.equationApproximate: Acceleration equals {force} newtons divided by {mass} kilograms, approximately {acceleration} meters per second squared
Newton.setup: Both start from rest, with force applied for 2 seconds

insights.zero: Zero net force means zero acceleration. The cart starts from rest, so it stays still.
insights.initial: Change the net force from 4 N to 8 N and watch the acceleration.
insights.doubleForce: Double the force with the same mass, and acceleration doubles. Speed increases by 4 m/s each second.
insights.doubleMass: Double the mass with the same force, and acceleration halves. Speed increases by 1 m/s each second.
insights.sameRatio: Force and mass change in the same proportion. Acceleration matches the reference: speed increases by 2 m/s each second.
insights.other: Speed increases by about {acceleration} m/s each second. Acceleration is about {ratio} times the reference.

Newton.assumptions: Compare horizontal motion only, ignoring friction. Both carts start from rest. Net force stays constant for 2 seconds.

status.complete: Comparison complete. After 2 seconds, your cart moves at {speed} meters per second; the reference moves at 4 meters per second.
status.ready: Net force: {force} newtons. Mass: {mass} kilograms. Acceleration: {acceleration} meters per second squared.

Newton.static: At constant mass, doubling net force doubles acceleration. At constant force, doubling mass halves acceleration. Enable JavaScript to adjust force and mass and observe both carts.
